candidate.answerReason: The pyramid has height \(1/\sqrt2\). Similar horizontal sections give cube side \(s=1-\sqrt2s\), so \(s=\sqrt2-1\) and its volume is \(5\sqrt2-7\).

methods.label: Use a horizontal square section
methods.explanation:
The cube's upper face is horizontal, so a section of the pyramid parallel to its base will determine the cube's side length.

Let \(S\) be the apex and \(O\) the center of the square base. Every lateral edge has length 1 because the lateral faces are equilateral. The perpendicular projection of \(S\) onto the base is equidistant from all four base vertices, so it is \(O\). The distance from \(O\) to a base vertex is half the square's diagonal, or \(\sqrt2/2\). Hence the pyramid's height \(H\) satisfies
\[
H^2+\left(\frac{\sqrt2}{2}\right)^2=1,
\qquad H=\frac1{\sqrt2}.
\]

Let the cube's side length be \(s\), where \(0<s<H\). Its upper face is at height \(s\). Each lateral face meets that horizontal plane in one side of a square section. Since all four upper edges of the cube lie on the lateral faces, the cube's upper face must be exactly that section.

By similar triangles in vertical sections through the apex, the horizontal square's side length is scaled from the base by \((H-s)/H\). Therefore
\[
s=\frac{H-s}{H}=1-\sqrt2s,
\]
so
\[
s=\frac1{1+\sqrt2}=\sqrt2-1.
\]
This is positive and smaller than \(H\). Centering the cube beneath this section gives a valid placement, since the pyramid's sections become larger below it.

The volume is
\[
s^3=(\sqrt2-1)^3=\boxed{5\sqrt2-7},
\]
which is choice \(\boxed{\text{A}}\).
